payload.summary: The finding is fully addressed: review lanes now face unconditional Phase 6, 95% progress, work-item, and terminal status gates. The adopted implementation anchor requires provenance, while green acceptance and evidence gates still prevent adoption with unevidenced criteria. The four tests cover these paths.

findings: acceptance_not_met: Specify that design-lane advance 3 and init --from-design retain every Phase 1–3 gate, including human design approval where required, and that all lane refusals preflight without mutation.

incorrect_implementation: Define init --lane review --adopt behavior when the resolved commit author is missing or unknown: refuse before writing, or persist a verifiable identity that the Phase 6 independence gate can compare; never permit review with an unenforceable implementer identity.
payload.summary: The proposal is directionally sound but leaves two integrity-critical behaviors undefined: preservation of the existing Phase 3 approval gate and unknown commit-author handling for review lanes.

approach: Data shape: status fields lane (full|design|review), phases_run and phases_waived (sorted disjoint integer arrays 1..8), inherited_waived (sorted integer array), implementation_adopted, taken_up_from, design_document, review_report (nullable objects); records are bounded and trust-hashed where stated.

Keep lane entry and phase gates in the shared library, with supervisor commands re-checking them so hand-crafted status cannot enter Phase 3; require a real approved non-Architect review bound to the current design hash.
Use design.html with schema version 1 and one canonical sorted-key JSON block; validate the block before rendering deterministic human-readable HTML from it, never parse the block from page prose.

Preflight all lane refusals before mutation and require status, acceptance, and both ledgers to remain byte-identical; write design.html and review_report.md in the run root beside handsoff-status.json.
Make archive analysis select only rules for phases in phases_run; waived phases are never treated as passed and no lane-specific rule loosens an existing gate.
constraints: Patch release only; preserve behavior for existing runs without a lane field.
Use only the acceptance commands already present in handsoff.toml.
Implement within bin/handsoff_lib.py, bin/handsoff_supervisor.py, schemas/, dashboard/, and targeted tests.
decisions: Legacy status without lane remains full-lane with unchanged behavior.
Lane values are full, design, or review; phases_run and phases_waived are sorted, disjoint, and cover the lane decision explicitly.
Design entry reaches Phase 3 only with matching criteria hash and an approved independent non-Architect review; matching hash without approval reaches Phase 2.
Review entry adopts a resolved commit and starts at Phase 5; it exits at Phase 6 and never deploys.
payload.summary: Add explicit design and review lanes while preserving full-lane behavior for legacy runs and enforcing complete phase gates for every phase a lane runs.
tradeoffs: Persisting explicit waived and inherited phase state increases status and ledger detail but makes skipped work auditable and preserves trust-chain intent.
Keeping machine-readable JSON separate from rendered prose makes round-tripping deterministic and prevents page edits from becoming evidence.
Run-root artifacts simplify ownership, hashing, and archival at the cost of keeping generated documents inside each run directory.
